title: U.S. House · Wisconsin's 5th Congressional District
area: Southeastern Wisconsin, including Waukesha and Jefferson counties west of Milwaukee.

context.text: Incumbent Scott Fitzgerald (R) advanced unopposed from the Republican primary. Andrew Beck advanced from the Democratic primary after Ben Steinhoff withdrew.

candidates.name: Scott Fitzgerald
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Republican primary unopposed.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for Wisconsin's 5th Congressional District (since 2021)

summary.text: Scott Fitzgerald is the Republican incumbent representing Wisconsin's 5th District since 2021. A newspaper owner and Army Reserve officer, he served in the Wisconsin State Senate from 1995 to 2021, including as majority leader, before winning the seat vacated by Jim Sensenbrenner. He serves on the Financial Services and Judiciary committees and chairs a Judiciary subcommittee.

background.text: Born in Chicago in 1963; later moved to Wisconsin and graduated from Hustisford High School in 1981. Earned a Bachelor of Science from the University of Wisconsin-Oshkosh in 1985 (journalism, according to Ballotpedia).

Joined the U.S. Army Reserve in 1981, was commissioned a lieutenant in the Armor Branch in 1985, completed the Army Command and General Staff College, served as a battalion commander, and retired in 2009 as a lieutenant colonel.
Bought the Dodge County Independent News in Juneau, Wisconsin, in 1990 and sold it in 1996 to the Watertown Daily Times, where he remained as an associate publisher for a number of years.

Served in the Wisconsin State Senate representing the 13th District from 1995 to 2021. His official biography lists him as Majority Leader, Minority Leader, Co-Chairman of the Joint Committee on Finance and Chairman of the Senate Corrections Committee; Ballotpedia lists him as majority leader in 2004 and from 2011 to 2020.

Comes from a family in public service: his father, Stephen Fitzgerald, was Dodge County sheriff, a U.S. Marshal and Wisconsin State Patrol superintendent, and his brother Jeff was Speaker of the Wisconsin State Assembly in the 2011-2012 session.

Elected to the U.S. House in 2020 for the seat vacated by retiring Republican Rep. Jim Sensenbrenner, defeating Democrat Tom Palzewicz 60.1% to 39.8%; he won re-election in 2022 and 2024 with 64.4% each time.

Serves on the House Financial Services Committee (Financial Institutions; Housing and Insurance; Task Force on Monetary Policy, Treasury Market Resilience, and Economic Prosperity) and the Judiciary Committee, where he chairs the Subcommittee on the Administrative State, Regulatory Reform, and Antitrust and sits on the Courts, Intellectual Property, Artificial Intelligence, and the Internet Subcommittee.
His official biography says he and his wife, Lisa, live in rural Clyman, where they raise horses, and have three sons.

priorities.text: Campaign materials say he led the fight for Act 10, right-to-work legislation, and balanced budgets in Wisconsin, and that he is a proven ally for President Trump in fixing problems in Washington.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Financial Services and the House Committee on the Judiciary, chairing the Administrative State, Regulatory Reform, and Antitrust Subcommittee, in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.researchNotes: The cited key campaign messages on Ballotpedia are compiled from his 2020 campaign materials; no updated 2026 statement of positions was found.

candidates.name: Andrew Beck
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Democratic primary after Ben Steinhoff withdrew.

summary.text: Andrew "Andy" Beck is the Democratic nominee for Wisconsin's 5th District. A Milwaukee native who lives in West Bend, he has worked in hotel management and in sales and management roles in the health care technology industry, and has a background as an MRI technologist. This is his first run for public office; his campaign priorities include lowering prescription drug costs, expanding affordable health care, increasing housing construction and protecting democracy.

background.text: Born and raised in Milwaukee, Wisconsin; graduated from Washington High School and attended Milwaukee Public Schools, according to his announcement and Ballotpedia survey.

Earned a bachelor's degree in hospitality management from the University of Wisconsin-Stout (1990, per Ballotpedia), a certificate in radiologic technology from the Froedtert School of Radiologic Technology, and an MBA from Cardinal Stritch University (2001, per Ballotpedia).
According to his campaign announcement, held management roles at Hilton Hotels, GE Healthcare and Hologic; Ballotpedia lists his career experience as sales manager and MRI technologist.
Describes himself as a healthcare professional and business leader, and as the son of Wisconsin's union movement.
Lives in West Bend and has lived in the 5th District for over 20 years, according to the Watertown Daily Times.
Announced his candidacy in October 2025 as his first run for public office; became the Democratic nominee after fellow Democrat Ben Steinhoff withdrew.

priorities.text: Names democracy as his top priority, saying protecting it is essential before other issues can be addressed.
priorities.quote: Democracy - Protecting our democracy is the single most important issue we need to address today.

priorities.text: Says everyone deserves the best healthcare the U.S. can provide at a practical price, with a focus on mental health access.
Says the country needs to continue working on policies to reduce the effects of global warming, including reducing greenhouse gases.

positions.summary: Candidate survey says a woman's right to decide her own healthcare choices is paramount.
Candidate survey names reducing greenhouse gases and addressing global warming as among his top three campaign priorities.
Candidate survey says everyone deserves the best healthcare the U.S. can provide at a practical price, with easy access, and highlights mental health treatment.

candidates.researchNotes: Beck has not held elected office, so there is no official voting or legislative record.
